headline: Tech and bitcoin bounce as Big Tech earnings season kicks off
summary: Bitcoin climbed back above $84,000 and altcoins like Zcash, Ethena and NEAR jumped double digits, though ether funds keep bleeding money. Stocks are modestly higher, led by tech after SpaceX's big beat, with the TSX up 0.7% on banks and energy. Meta and Tesla report tonight, and both the Fed and the Bank of Canada decide on rates next Wednesday.

crypto.label: Mixed
crypto.why: Prices are bouncing and the Fear & Greed index reads 63 (Greed), but ether ETF outflows and bitcoin's tight link to tech stocks keep the rally fragile.

stocks.label: Cautious
stocks.why: Earnings are solid and the VIX is easing, but a 5.1% 10-year yield, oil near $100 and two central bank decisions next week keep investors careful.

drivers.title: Big Tech earnings season starts strong
drivers.detail: SpaceX beat forecasts handily and Super Micro raised its sales outlook, lifting tech; Netflix fell on weak guidance. Meta and Tesla report tonight, with Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon next week.

drivers.title: High yields and a Fed on hold
drivers.detail: The 10-year Treasury yield is about 5.1% after September CPI came in hot at 3.7%. Markets see about an 85% chance the Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28.

drivers.title: Oil near five-month highs on Iran tension
drivers.detail: Brent is around $108–$110 as Iran drags out talks with the U.S. and tension continues near the Strait of Hormuz; mediation rumours briefly knocked prices lower. The U.S. oil price on the dashboard looks down about 4%, but that is mostly a switch to the December contract.

drivers.title: Crypto ETF flows split
drivers.detail: Spot bitcoin ETFs took in about $527 million on Monday but are roughly flat-to-negative for October. Ether ETFs have lost about $1.08 billion this month, their worst month since November 2025.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada likely to hold
drivers.detail: Canadian headline inflation rose to 3.1% on gas prices, but core measures eased below 2%. Economists expect the Bank to hold at 2.25% on Oct. 28.

drivers.title: Tesla–SpaceX merger talk
drivers.detail: Musk said both companies formed special committees to study a combination that would pool more than 30,000 bitcoin. It is early-stage, with no terms yet.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Up 2.5% in 24h and 2.6% this week, to about $84,400 (still down about 1% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin bounced off the $82,500 area that traders had flagged as key support and climbed back above $84,000 as U.S. tech stocks firmed on SpaceX's earnings beat. Spot bitcoin ETFs (exchange-traded funds that hold real bitcoin) took in about $527 million on Monday, the biggest day since September, led by BlackRock's IBIT, though October is still slightly negative overall. Talk that SpaceX and Tesla are studying a merger that would pool more than 30,000 BTC on their balance sheets added to the upbeat tone.
crypto.meaning: Bitcoin is trading more like a tech stock right now, so Big Tech earnings and bond yields matter as much as crypto news. It is about a third below its October 2025 record of roughly $126,000, and the past month has been a range rather than a trend.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above $84,000 and then clearing the 20-day average near $83,100 decisively, plus steady ETF inflows and a calm Fed meeting on Oct. 28, could open a run at about $87,500, where bitcoin started 2026.
outlook.bearCase: A daily close back under the 50-day average near $81,700, and especially a break below $82,500 support, would revive the downside case some analysts and market maker Wintermute have outlined toward about $70,000; disappointing Tesla or Meta results could be the trigger.
outlook.watch: Daily ETF flow data, Tesla and Meta results tonight, the 10-year Treasury yield near 5.1%, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Up 2.8% in 24h and 1.6% this week, to about $2,500, but down 8.8% over 30 days
crypto.why: Ether rose with bitcoin after bouncing off the $2,400 area for several straight sessions. The bigger story is persistent selling by U.S. ether ETFs: roughly $1.08 billion has left since Oct. 1, the largest monthly outflow since November 2025, wiping out September's inflows. On the positive side, a record 43.8 million ETH (about 36% of supply) was staked in Q3, meaning locked up to help secure the network in exchange for rewards.
crypto.meaning: Ether has been the weaker of the two big coins all year (down nearly 18% in 2026). Bounces have struggled to stick while big funds keep withdrawing, so ETF flows are the clearest tell for whether this rebound has legs.

outlook.bullCase: If ETF outflows stop and ether holds above $2,500, a move toward roughly $2,700, where October began, becomes plausible, helped by any broad risk-on lift from tech earnings.
outlook.bearCase: Continued ETF selling and a clean break below $2,400 would put the year's lows back in view and likely extend ether's underperformance versus bitcoin.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,400 floor, the ETH/BTC ratio, and the Fed meeting on Oct. 28.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Up 11.6% in 24h and 9.8% this week, to about $1,330 (still down 13.6% over 30 days)
crypto.why: The privacy coin jumped as traders positioned for its NU7 network upgrade, which would cut block times from 75 to 25 seconds and steer 60% of fees to a treasury; CoinDesk reported a November date is now set, with one analyst pointing to Nov. 6. Bitwise's Zcash ETF also logged fresh inflows. Zcash has been one of 2026's biggest winners and now sits in the top 10 by market value.
crypto.meaning: Zcash moves in big swings both ways: it is up enormously this year but fell sharply over the past month before this bounce. Upgrade rallies often peak around the event itself, so the run-up can reverse quickly.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the breakout above about $1,180 and clearing resistance near $1,300 could carry it toward the $1,650–$1,700 area some technical analysts are watching into the upgrade.
outlook.bearCase: A 'sell the news' fade or a delay to NU7 could send it back below $1,180 and toward the $1,000 area; heavy use of borrowed money (leverage) in privacy coins makes sharp drops more likely.
outlook.watch: Confirmation of the NU7 activation date, ETF flows, and whether $1,180 holds on pullbacks.

crypto.name: Ethena
crypto.move: Up 13.0% in 24h and 5.5% this week, to about $0.216 (down 6.8% over 30 days)
crypto.why: ENA led large-cap gainers, but coverage today points to technical momentum rather than a single news event; the hourly RSI, a gauge of how overstretched a move is, hit about 73, which is considered overbought. A longer-term support is that the last tranche of early-investor tokens unlocked on Oct. 5, ending Ethena's monthly investor unlocks after the foundation bought out many early backers in August.
crypto.meaning: With the investor unlock overhang gone, ENA's supply picture is cleaner, but USDe, the synthetic dollar that drives Ethena's revenue, is far below its 2025 peak. A one-day pop on no clear news can unwind just as fast.

outlook.bullCase: A sustained move above about $0.2165, with USDe supply growing again, could carry ENA toward the mid-$0.20s.
outlook.bearCase: If the overbought bounce fades, a drop under about $0.195 (its 50-day average) would erase this week's gains.
outlook.watch: USDe supply, the $0.195–$0.2165 range, and broader altcoin risk appetite.

crypto.name: NEAR Protocol
crypto.move: Up 10.6% in 24h, 6.5% this week and 27.6% over 30 days, to about $5.34
crypto.why: NEAR has been one of October's strongest large coins. Supports include the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF from Bitwise (launched Sept. 29), a governance proposal to cut yearly new-token issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%, and strong use of its NEAR Intents cross-chain swap service. Today's jump came without a single fresh headline and fits a broad altcoin bounce.
crypto.meaning: The rally has real drivers behind it, but the issuance cut is only a proposal and NEAR is already back near its early-October highs around $6. Fast multi-week runs tend to see sharp pullbacks.

outlook.bullCase: Approval of the issuance cut and continued ETF inflows could push NEAR back to test the $5.60–$6.00 area hit earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: If momentum fades or the proposal stalls, a pullback toward roughly $4.50–$5.00 would be typical after a run this size.
outlook.watch: The issuance-cut vote, NEAR ETF flows, and whether $5 holds.

sources.title: Crypto Briefing: NEAR jumps on record trading

crypto.name: Worldcoin
crypto.move: Up 1.6% in 24h, 16.4% this week and 29% over 30 days, to about $0.57
crypto.why: World unveiled World ID tools for banking and finance at the Money20/20 conference, including identity checks and protection against video impersonation and AI agents. Futures open interest jumped and short sellers were forced to buy back (a 'short squeeze' via liquidations), which amplified the move earlier this week.
crypto.meaning: The product news is real, but part of the jump came from derivatives traders being squeezed, which does not prove lasting demand. WLD is still about 95% below its record high.

outlook.bullCase: Clearing resistance around $0.59–$0.62 with real partner announcements could target about $0.70.
outlook.bearCase: If leverage unwinds, a slide back to the $0.46–$0.47 support area is possible.
outlook.watch: Open interest and funding rates, partner rollouts of World ID, and the $0.59 level.

sources.title: CaptainAltcoin: Why are Zcash and Worldcoin pumping?

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Up 4.7% in 24h and 2.4% this week, to about $1.38 (down 7.2% over 30 days)
crypto.why: XRP outpaced bitcoin in today's broad altcoin bounce. Ripple's push to offer round-the-clock stock trading on crypto rails is in the news, though HSBC described demand for such products as thin so far, and no single XRP-specific catalyst explains today's gain.
crypto.meaning: XRP tends to move more than bitcoin in both directions, so today's outperformance mostly reflects higher risk appetite. The 30-day trend is still down.

outlook.bullCase: A broader crypto rally led by bitcoin holding above $84,000 could lift XRP back toward the $1.45–$1.50 area.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin slips back under $82,500, XRP would likely give back today's gains and retest about $1.30.
outlook.watch: Bitcoin's direction, U.S. regulatory steps on digital-asset rules, and Ripple product news.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Up 2.6% in 24h and 2.6% this week, to about $108 (down 8.9% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana moved roughly in line with the market as its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality, was set to go live on Wednesday. Big upgrades can attract buyers but also carry execution risk.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch would be a meaningful technical milestone, but price has lagged this month. Watch for any network problems in the first days after launch.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or a bitcoin drop below $82,500, could push SOL under $100.
outlook.watch: Network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $82,500–$84,000 zone, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: S&P 500
stocks.move: Up 0.35% to about 7,740 late morning, about 1.3% below its record high near 7,845
stocks.why: Stocks edged higher as Big Tech earnings season got going, helped by SpaceX's strong results and tech strength, while Netflix and Alphabet lagged. The VIX, Wall Street's 'fear gauge', slipped to about 16.7. The 10-year Treasury yield stayed high at about 5.1%, which caps how far valuations can stretch.
stocks.meaning: The index has spent October chopping below its record as high yields and oil above $95 compete with solid earnings. Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson thinks the pullback is nearly done but expects a few more weeks of turbulence; he targets 8,500 by mid-2027.

outlook.bullCase: Strong results from Meta and Tesla tonight and from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon next week, plus a calm Fed on Oct. 28, could push the index back to its record near 7,845.
outlook.bearCase: Disappointing AI spending guidance, a jump in the 10-year yield above recent highs near 5.3%, or a renewed oil spike could send it back toward the 7,600 area seen earlier this month.
outlook.watch: Big Tech earnings, the 10-year yield, oil prices and the Fed decision on Oct. 28.

stocks.name: Nasdaq Composite
stocks.move: Up 0.86% to about 26,650, about 3.9% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: Tech led today: SpaceX jumped after beating forecasts, Tesla rose on merger talk and chip stocks firmed after Super Micro raised its sales forecast sharply. Alphabet's slide trimmed the gain.
stocks.meaning: The Nasdaq is the most sensitive index to AI-spending headlines and to bond yields, so the next two weeks of megacap earnings will likely decide its direction. Crypto has been moving closely with it.

outlook.bullCase: Upbeat AI revenue and spending commentary from Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet could carry it back toward the 27,500–27,700 highs.
outlook.bearCase: Any sign that AI spending is slowing, or that returns are not showing up, could revive last week's chip selloff and push it back below 26,000.
outlook.watch: Meta and Tesla tonight, Alphabet and Microsoft on Oct. 28, Amazon on Oct. 29.

stocks.name: S&P/TSX Composite
stocks.move: Up 0.70% to about 36,360, about 1.9% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: Toronto outpaced Wall Street, with banks and energy names up: oil remains near five-month highs on Middle East tension, and major banks like TD and RBC gained about 1–1.5%. Miners lagged as gold and copper softened. The loonie also firmed to about 71.1 U.S. cents.
stocks.meaning: The TSX is heavy in banks, energy and miners, so it benefits from high oil and a steady Bank of Canada. Canada's inflation is 3.1% on the headline but the Bank's preferred core measures are below 2%, which supports another hold on Oct. 28.

outlook.bullCase: Oil holding near $100, a steady Bank of Canada on Oct. 28 and solid bank results could take the TSX back toward its 37,000 high.
outlook.bearCase: A sudden Iran deal that knocks oil sharply lower, or a global tech selloff, could pull it back to the 35,500 area.
outlook.watch: Oil and Iran headlines, the Bank of Canada decision on Oct. 28, and the loonie.

stocks.name: SpaceX
stocks.move: Up about 8.7% to about $160.60 as of 10:40 a.m. ET (up as much as 10% intraday)
stocks.why: SpaceX's third-quarter results beat forecasts: revenue was about $14.6 billion versus about $12.7 billion expected, and earnings per share were $0.35 versus $0.14. Its AI business brought in about $7.6 billion, more than Starlink and rockets combined. Elon Musk also said SpaceX and Tesla have set up special committees to study a possible merger.
stocks.meaning: The beat shows how central AI has become to SpaceX's story. A large lockup expiry on Thursday, when up to 1.3 billion early shares can be sold, could add selling pressure even after good news.

outlook.bullCase: If buyers absorb Thursday's unlocked shares and merger talks progress, traders are eyeing resistance around $172.
outlook.bearCase: Heavy selling from newly unlocked holders could push it back below support near $150.
outlook.watch: Thursday's lockup expiry, any merger details, and trading volume.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Up 3.2% to about $385.80 ahead of results after the close
stocks.why: Tesla rose after Musk said Tesla and SpaceX formed special committees to study a possible merger, which would combine more than 30,000 bitcoin across the two balance sheets. It also reports third-quarter results after the close today.
stocks.meaning: Tonight's numbers and any merger commentary could move the stock sharply either way. A merger is only being studied, and terms, valuation and approvals are all unknown.

outlook.bullCase: Better-than-expected margins or delivery guidance, plus concrete merger progress, could push it toward the $410–$420 area from earlier this year.
outlook.bearCase: Weak margins or skepticism over a related-party merger could send it back toward $355–$365.
outlook.watch: Earnings tonight, merger committee updates, and margin guidance.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Up 2.1% to about $709 ahead of results after the close
stocks.why: Meta bounced ahead of its third-quarter report after the bell, where analysts expect earnings of about $5.74 a share on revenue near $63.4 billion. The stock had slipped from the $760s earlier this month.
stocks.meaning: The key questions are ad growth and how much Meta plans to spend on AI data centres next year. Spending guidance has moved the stock more than profit in recent quarters.

outlook.bullCase: Strong ad growth with spending guidance investors can live with could send it back toward the $740–$780 range.
outlook.bearCase: A jump in planned spending without matching revenue growth could knock it back below $680.
outlook.watch: Revenue versus the roughly $63.4 billion estimate and 2027 spending guidance tonight.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.move: Down about 4% as of 10:40 a.m. ET, after falling over 6% in after-hours trading
stocks.why: Netflix's quarterly profit beat forecasts, but revenue was a hair light and its fourth-quarter revenue forecast missed estimates. It also cut its 2026 advertising revenue outlook.
stocks.meaning: Investors are focused on growth and the ad business, and both forecasts disappointed. Stocks that drop on guidance cuts often stay weak until the next report gives new information.

outlook.bullCase: Analysts defending the long-term story or a quick rebound in tech could limit the damage.
outlook.bearCase: More analyst target cuts could extend the slide over the coming days.
outlook.watch: Analyst rating changes and whether today's low holds.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.move: Down 2.3% to about $332.50, one of the weakest megacaps today
stocks.why: Investors trimmed positions ahead of Alphabet's Oct. 28 results, where expectations for Google Cloud and spending are high. KeyBanc cut its target to $410 from $435 (still Overweight), a Google Cloud data centre outage near London disrupted UK banks on Oct. 20, and law firms are promoting a class action over its Gemini model timeline.
stocks.meaning: None of these is a major business blow alone, but together they weigh on sentiment into earnings. The stock is near support around $332 and well below its $408 high.

outlook.bullCase: Strong cloud growth on Oct. 28 could quickly lift it back toward $345–$355.
outlook.bearCase: A clear break below about $332 support could send it toward the $317–$320 area seen in late summer.
outlook.watch: Q3 results on Oct. 28, cloud growth, and spending guidance.

stocks.name: Strategy
stocks.move: Up 7.2% to about $153, outpacing bitcoin's 2.5% gain
stocks.why: Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder with about 848,000 BTC, tends to move about two to three times as much as bitcoin. Today's jump tracks bitcoin's bounce above $84,000. Recent support includes continued bitcoin buying, a larger share-buyback authorization and a Barclays target raise to $175.
stocks.meaning: MSTR is effectively a leveraged bet on bitcoin, so it amplifies both gains and losses. Its moves today say more about bitcoin than about the company.

outlook.bullCase: Bitcoin holding above $84,000 and moving toward $87,500 could lift MSTR toward the $165 area.
outlook.bearCase: A bitcoin break below $82,500 would likely send MSTR back under $140.
outlook.watch: Bitcoin's direction, Strategy's weekly purchase filings, and its Q3 results.

stocks.meaning: Shopify is Canada's biggest tech stock and moves with U.S. tech sentiment. After a big run, expectations for its next results are high.

outlook.bullCase: Strong megacap earnings and early holiday-spending signals could push it through C$256 to new highs.
outlook.bearCase: A tech pullback could drag it back toward the C$235–C$240 area.
outlook.watch: Nasdaq direction, consumer-spending data, and its upcoming results.
